# Build Systems

## :dart: Learning goals of this lecture
- How can I manage my builds
- Get to know and work with `cmake`
:::

## Build system

As we could see from the previous example, building a project can be a complex and requires the following steps:

- Check if all dependencies are available, if not install them
- Check for problems within the code (Lint)
- Build required libraries
- Build executable
- Run tests
- Create documentation

## Project structure

Having an appropriate project structure helps to keep the overview.
```{.bash code-line-numbers="false"}
$ tree project
project/
|-- CMakeLists.txt
|-- include
|   +-- math_utils.hpp
|-- src
|   |-- main.cpp
|   +-- math_utils.cpp
+-- tests
    +-- math_utils.test.cpp

4 directories, 5 files
```

## Building with cmake 1/3

```{python}
#| echo: false
%%bash
cd code/project
echo "$ cmake -S . -B build"
cmake -S . -B build
```

## Building with cmake 2/3

```{python}
#| echo: false
%%bash
cd code/project
echo "$ cmake --build build"
cmake --build build
```

## Building with cmake 3/3

```{python}
#| echo: false
%%bash
cd code/project
echo "$ build/main"
build/main
```

```{.cpp}
install(TARGETS main math_utils DESTINATION bin)
install(FILES include/math_utils.h DESTINATION include)
```

## How to include {.smaller}


| **Form** | **Search Order** | **Use Case** |
|--|---|---|
| `#include <header>` | System include paths only | Standard library headers or third-party libraries installed in system paths. |
| `#include "header"` | Current directory first, then system include paths | Project-specific headers or headers in the same directory. |
| `#include <folder/header>` | System include paths only | Third-party libraries with organized subdirectories. |
| `#include "folder/header"` | Current directory first, then system include paths | Project-specific headers in subdirectories. |
| `#include <absolute/path>` | No search; directly includes the file from the specified absolute path | Rarely used; for debugging or non-standard locations. |
| `#include "relative/path"` | Current directory or relative to the file, then system include paths | Headers in parent or sibling directories. |
